author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island’s Office of the Child Advocate says the state’s child-protection system needs immediate changes after a review identified persistent weaknesses in screening, staffing and prevention services.

The review covered 30 fatalities and 11 near-fatalities involving children with current or prior Department of Children, Youth and Families contact. Child Advocate Katelyn Medeiros said reviewers found cases that should have been accepted for investigation but were screened out, along with families who sought help but were not connected to prevention services.

The report contains 76 recommendations spanning Child Protective Services practices, the Support and Response Unit, oversight and longer-term system improvements. Investigators also found caseloads above national best-practice levels and delays in responding to families within the department’s own timelines.

Medeiros said staffing is part of the problem but not the only answer; policy, law, regulation and internal systems also need better alignment. The findings describe a reform agenda rather than completed changes. Accountability will depend on which recommendations DCYF accepts, the timeline for implementation and whether lawmakers or administrators provide the necessary authority and resources.
dek: A review of 30 fatalities and 11 near-fatalities identified inconsistent screening, high caseloads and missed opportunities to connect families with help.
headline: Rhode Island child advocate calls for immediate child-protection changes
